title: InterpolatedDistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a convex population objective f over all of ℝᵈ. At every oracle step k, f is the pointwise expectation of integrable convex C∞ sample losses. All sample losses share a global minimizer u with ‖x₀−u‖≤R.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query at x returns one sample gradient g(x,ξ) using a fresh i.i.d. seed. Its mean belongs to ∂f(x). Every sample returns the same vector g₀ at x₀ and zero at u. The algorithm receives the gradient vector. The sample loss, seed, sampling law, u, and g₀ are outside the public input.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/InterpolatedDistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, Interpolates; LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.publicInput and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Public and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The same oracle also accepts a projection query. Euclidean projection onto the whole space returns the query point. Each gradient or projection query uses one call from the same fixed budget. The setup permits arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Query and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/InterpolatedDistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, Interpolates; LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec; LongTails/Template.lean, Setup.allowedAlgorithm, Algorithm and executeWithTrace.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: The raw second moment satisfies E‖g(x,ξ)‖²≤G²+B²‖x−x₀‖² for every x. This permits heavy tails and bounds the second moment in terms of distance from the public starting point.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain is the full Euclidean space ℝᵈ for every public dimension d≥2.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Vector and Public; LongTails/Setups/InterpolatedDistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, Interpolates and spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Interpolation and exact agreement at initialization hold simultaneously for every step and every seed. The C∞ condition on sample losses specifies no uniform Lipschitz constant for their gradients. The public parameters are d, x₀, B, G, R, ε, and δ, with B≥0, G,R,ε>0, 65536ε≤GR, and 0<δ≤1/8.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The terminal output x̂ must be measurable and feasible for every realization. Its target is f(x̂)−f(x⋆)≤ε for a global minimizer x⋆. The algorithm may output any point computed from its state.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.successful; LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.output and execute.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Under the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle seed sequence, Pr[f(x̂)−f(x⋆)>ε]≤δ.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Every sample gradient agrees at the public starting point and vanishes at a shared hidden minimizer, while its second moment elsewhere can grow quadratically with distance from the starting point.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Interpolation with Distance-Growing Subgradients

We minimize an expected loss f on Euclidean space Rd of dimension d≥2. The smooth convex sample losses share a minimizer x⋆ and have the same gradient at the given starting point x0. The oracle returns a sample gradient using a fresh independent draw, or the query point itself for a projection query. The gradient’s second moment is bounded by an affine function of squared distance from x0. For tolerance ε>0 and failure probability δ∈(0,1/8], the goal is a measurable output x¯ satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x). The algorithm receives d,x0,B,G,R,ε,δ, where B≥0 and G>0 control the second moment, R>0 bounds the initial distance to a common minimizer, and 65536ε≤GR. At call k=0,1,…, the oracle uses a sample Zk from a sequence of independent, identically distributed random variables with law ν on a measurable space Z. The sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Interpolating sample losses). For each k and z∈Z, the loss ℓk,z:Rd→R is convex and C∞. There exist x⋆,g0∈Rd with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R such that, for every k and z, ℓk,z(x⋆)=minx∈Rdℓk,z(x),∇ℓk,z(x0)=g0. For every k and x, ℓk,Zk(x) is integrable and the measurable convex objective satisfies f(x)=E[ℓk,Zk(x)]. In particular, x⋆ minimizes f.

Assumption 2 (Distance-dependent second moment). The subgradient reply at x on call k is g(x,Zk), where g:Rd×Z→Rd is jointly measurable and g(x,z)=∇ℓk,z(x) for every k,x,z. For each x and Z∼ν, the vector g(x,Z) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,Z)∥2 is integrable. For all x,y∈Rd, f(x)−f(y)≤⟨E[g(x,Z)],x−y⟩,E[∥g(x,Z)∥2]≤B2∥x−x0∥2+G2.

Both query types accept any x∈Rd and count toward the same call budget. After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be a measurable Rd-valued random variable satisfying P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε)≥1−δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, d≥2, the convex C∞ sample losses have mean f, share a minimizer u with ∥x0−u∥≤R, and have identical gradients at x0. With IID samples, the jointly measurable sample gradient g(x) satisfies Eg(x)∈∂f(x) and E∥g(x)∥2≤G2+B2∥x−x0∥2 for every x. Here G,R>0, B≥0, 0<ε≤GR/65536, and 0<δ≤1/8. The target for any randomized adaptive algorithm is Pr[f(x^)−f(u)>ε]≤δ on every instance.

Necessary oracle budgets for interpolating convex losses with distance-growing gradient moments.

(1) requires d≥2, ε≤GR/65536, δ≤1/8. Its hard instances have sample smoothness of order (G2+B2R2)/ε. (2) allows access to entire sample losses.

Abbr: Each sample-gradient or identity-projection query counts as one call in (1). In (2), the budget counts independent samples.

import LongTails.Setups.DistanceGrowingSubgradient
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

open scoped ContDiff
open MeasureTheory OracleTemplate
open LongTails.Setups.TerminalClippingConvex

namespace LongTails.Setups.InterpolatedDistanceGrowingSubgradient

def Interpolates (p : Public) (I : Instance p) (O : Oracle (Query p) (Vector p.d) 1) : Prop :=
  I.domain = Set.univ ∧
  ∃ (u g₀ : Vector p.d) (loss : (k : ℕ) → O.Seed k → Vector p.d → ℝ),
    ‖p.x0 - u‖ ≤ p.R ∧
    (∀ k z, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (loss k z) ∧ ContDiff ℝ ∞ (loss k z) ∧
      IsMinOn (loss k z) Set.univ u) ∧
    (∀ k z, gradient (loss k z) p.x0 = g₀) ∧
    (∀ h x z, O.answer h (0, .subgradient x) z = gradient (loss h.length z) x) ∧
    ∀ k x, Integrable (fun ξ : (i : ℕ) → O.Seed i => loss k (ξ k) x) (O.law : Measure _) ∧
      I.f x = ∫ (ξ : (i : ℕ) → O.Seed i), loss k (ξ k) x ∂(O.law : Measure _)

abbrev spec : Setup :=
  { DistanceGrowingSubgradient.spec with
    valid := fun p => 2 ≤ p.d ∧ 0 ≤ p.B ∧ 0 < p.G ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
      65536 * p.ε ≤ p.G * p.R ∧ 0 < p.δ ∧ p.δ ≤ 1 / 8
    admissible := fun p I O => DistanceGrowingSubgradient.spec.admissible p I O ∧
      Interpolates p I O }

end LongTails.Setups.InterpolatedDistanceGrowingSubgradient
